card.name: Manipuri
card.era: Roots in ritual traditions; raslila formalized 18th century
card.tagline: Manipur's gentle devotional classical dance of Krishna's raslila
card.profile: Manipuri dance is a major Indian classical dance form from the northeastern state of Manipur, distinguished by gentle, fluid, gliding movements in which the feet rarely strike the floor hard (Wikipedia). A confluence of ritual traditions - Lai Haraoba, Huyen Langlon, Nata Sankirtana and Raslila - its best-known expression is the Raas Leela depicting the love of Krishna, Radha and the gopis, alongside the vigorous male Pung Cholom drum dance (Wikipedia). The dance is devotional in nature, rooted in Vaishnavism with themes also from Shaktism and Shaivism.
card.insight: Under King Bhagyachandra (Ching Thang Khomba) in the 18th century the raslila was formalized, and Manipuri gained wider recognition after poet Rabindranath Tagore witnessed a performance in 1917 and introduced its teaching at Visva-Bharati, Santiniketan (Britannica).
